## 0. Inputs, standing hypotheses, and standard theorems

**Standing hypotheses.** (CE), (BAL), (N) are exactly the hypotheses of ATT-0088: (CE) the standard degree-four Casnati-Ekedahl ideal resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0 on X=P(E^vee) with p_*O_X(1)=E; (BAL) the relations bundle F is fibrewise O(4)+O(5); (N) O_X(1)|_C = omega_{C/P1} tensor gamma^*A for some A in Pic(P1). (N) is the packet's undischarged weak relative-canonical normalization (FND-0105); it is carried as a hypothesis of every clause that uses it and is never asserted.

**Verified dependencies (cited, used inside their stated scope).** ATT-0065 (C66-GEO-Z), dual-confirmed by REV-0108 and REV-0109: CLM-0065-1, CLM-0065-3, CLM-0065-4, CLM-0065-5, CLM-0065-9 give the filtered CE reduction and the identification of the evaluation-failure scheme with the relative Abel-Jacobi incidence O(Gamma) = W_5 tensor omega^{-1}, scheme-theoretically and under arbitrary base change, on a base carrying six pairwise-disjoint sections. ATT-0066 (C66-GEO-H0), dual-confirmed by REV-0110 and REV-0116: CLM-0066-1, CLM-0066-2, CLM-0066-4, CLM-0066-5, CLM-0066-6 give h^0(L) in {3,4}, the closed Abel-Jacobi/Hilbert model, the projective-bundle model on a reduced constant-h^0 stratum, and the stack-level finite etale S_6-torsor over the reduced-support open. Verified supporting context: ATT-0086 (C66-COMP-COMP), dual-confirmed by REV-0135 and REV-0138: the jump stratum is empty, so h^0(L)=3 on every balanced (N)-normalized fibre; ATT-0088 (C66-COMP-RANK), dual-confirmed by REV-0139 and REV-0142: CLM-0088-1 (A trivial, W_5 = omega_C^2(-D), L = omega_C(-D)), CLM-0088-2 (no balanced fibre is hyperelliptic), CLM-0088-3 (h^0(O(D))=2, h^0(L)=3, h^1(L)=2), CLM-0088-5 (the reduced-support open of |L| is nonempty and dense, its complement is a curve, and the ordered incidence is a nonempty smooth degree-720 finite etale S_6-torsor), CLM-0088-8 (over a reduced base, AJ = P_S(pi_*L) is a P2-bundle, its reduced-support open U is S-smooth of relative dimension two and surjective, Z is the S_6-torsor of orderings over U, Z->S is smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two, and over a finite-type base every component of Z and of U dominates a component of S with dimension that of the dominated component plus two).

**Source input.** SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 as excerpted in the packet: the convention W_f = (O_X(2) tensor gamma^*O(-f))|_C with the minus sign, deg(W_f|_C) = 4g+12-4f, and deg(O_X(1)|_C) = 2g-2+4*2 = 18 at g=6.

**Standard theorems used without reproof.** Riemann-Roch and Serre duality on smooth curves; Clifford's theorem with its equality cases; relative duality for a finite flat morphism, gamma_*(omega_{C/P1}) = (gamma_*O_C)^vee; relative duality on a P2-bundle, R^2p_*(omega_{X/P1}) = O; Grothendieck's theorem that every vector bundle on P1 splits; Grauert's criterion over a reduced base; the base-point-free pencil trick; Castelnuovo-Severi together with the divisibility step for a common intermediate factor (FND-0135 discipline); in characteristic zero, reflexivity (biduality) of a plane curve, generic injectivity of its Gauss map, and finiteness of its flexes and of its multiply tangent lines; the local structure of a degree-two map of smooth surfaces branched along a smooth divisor; Jordan's theorem that a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a transposition is S_n; and invariance of the geometric etale fundamental group of a finite-type variety under extension of algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero (so the monodromy computations may be performed over C).

**Independence.** Every fibrewise statement below is proved from these standard inputs; where a packet adjudicated finding (FND-0105, FND-0125, FND-0130, FND-0134, FND-0139, FND-0142) records the same conclusion, it is quoted only as corroboration. No finite computation is used to prove any universal claim; the two explicit families in Section 6 are used only for existence statements, where a single verified instance is a proof.

## 1. The relative-canonical graded module

Write A_C := omega_{C/P1} = omega_C tensor gamma^*O(2), of degree 10+8 = 18. SRC-0004 records deg(O_X(1)|_C) = 18, while (N) gives degree 18 + 4 deg(A); hence deg(A) = 0 and, since Pic(P1) = Z, A = O. Therefore

  O_X(1)|_C = A_C,  W_f = A_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(-f),  W_4 = omega_C^2, W_5 = omega_C^2(-D), L = W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} = omega_C(-D),

with deg W_4 = 20, deg W_5 = 16, deg L = 6 and chi(L) = 1. This is (A0) first part and reproves ATT-0088/CLM-0088-1.

Euler characteristics fix the two ranks and degrees. From gamma_*O_C = O + E^vee and chi(O_C) = -5 one gets 1 + (3 - deg E) = -5, so deg E = 9. Relative duality gives gamma_*A_C = (gamma_*O_C)^vee = O + E, so chi(gamma_*A_C^2) = chi(A_C^2) = 36-5 = 31 and deg(gamma_*A_C^2) = 31-4 = 27, while Sym^2 E has rank 6 and degree 4*9 = 36.

Tensoring (CE) by O_X(2) and using Rp_*O_X(-2) = 0 on P2-fibres gives p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) = F and R^{>0}p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2)) = 0; applying p_* to 0->I_C(2)->O_X(2)->i_*(A_C^2)->0 yields the exact sequence on P1

  (1.1)  0 -> F -> Sym^2 E -> gamma_*(A_C^2) -> 0,

so F is the bundle of relative quadrics through C, of rank 6-4 = 2 and degree 36-27 = 9. (This is the packet's own description of F as ker(Sym^2E -> gamma_*R), recorded among the established working-context facts.) Since bundles on P1 split, F = O(a)+O(b) with a+b = 9 and a <= b, hence a <= 4 <= 5 <= b and

  (1.2)  h^0(F(-6)) = h^0(O(a-6)) + h^0(O(b-6)) = b-5,

because a-6 <= -2. Thus F is balanced precisely when h^0(F(-6)) = 0. This is (A0).

Next, tensor (CE) by O_X(1). Now Rp_*O_X(-1) = 0 in all degrees, while for the P2-bundle omega_{X/P1} = O_X(-3) tensor p^*det E, so R^2p_*O_X(-3) = det E^{-1} and R^{<2}p_*O_X(-3) = 0. The resolution therefore gives p_*(I_C(1)) = 0 and R^1p_*(I_C(1)) = det E^{-1} tensor det F, which is O_{P1} because deg det F = 9 = deg det E and line bundles on P1 are determined by their degree. Pushing forward 0->I_C(1)->O_X(1)->i_*A_C->0 yields

  (1.3)  0 -> E -> gamma_*A_C -> O -> 0.

Consequently, for every j <= -1 the restriction map is an isomorphism

  (1.4)  M_j := H^0(P1, E(j)) --~--> H^0(C, A_C tensor gamma^*O(j)) = H^0(C, omega_C((2+j)D)),

since H^0(O(j)) = 0. Explicitly M_{-2} = H^0(omega_C) (dimension 6), M_{-3} = H^0(L) , M_{-4} = H^0(omega_C(-2D)), M_{-5} = H^0(omega_C(-3D)) = 0 because deg(omega_C-3D) = -2. All these identifications are induced by restriction to C, hence are compatible with multiplication: the maps p_*O_X(m) -> gamma_*(A_C^m) come from a homomorphism of graded algebras, so a product of sections restricts to the product of the restrictions. This is the only structural input used in Section 3.

## 2. The Tschirnhausen splitting type

Assume (H3): h^0(L) = 3.

First, C is not hyperelliptic. If it were, then by Castelnuovo-Severi (g <= (2-1)(4-1) = 3 < 6 for independent maps) together with the divisibility step (a common intermediate factor phi has deg phi dividing 2 and at least 2, so phi is the hyperelliptic map and the residual map has degree one) we get gamma = q o h with deg q = 2, hence D = 2H for the hyperelliptic class H, omega_C = 5H, and h^0(L) = h^0(3H) = 4, contradicting (H3). Since deg(omega_C-2D) = 2, non-hyperellipticity gives h^0(omega_C(-2D)) <= 1.

Write E = O(e_1)+O(e_2)+O(e_3) with e_1+e_2+e_3 = 9. By (1.4), h^0(E(-m)) = sum_i max(0, e_i-m+1) equals h^0(omega_C((2-m)D)); at m = 5, 4, 3 this reads

  sum_i max(0,e_i-4) = 0,  sum_i max(0,e_i-3) = h^0(omega_C(-2D)),  sum_i max(0,e_i-2) = 3.

The first equation gives e_i <= 4 for all i. If some e_i <= 1 then the remaining two are 4,4 and the third sum is 0+2+2 = 4, not 3; hence e_i >= 2 for all i, and then the third equation is automatic. The only partitions of 9 with all parts in [2,4] are (3,3,3) and (2,3,4), and the middle equation distinguishes them:

  (2.1)  E = O(3)^3 <=> h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = 0,  E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4) <=> h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = 1.

For comparison (not used below), in the hyperelliptic-composed case h^0(L) = 4, h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = h^0(H) = 2 and the same three equations force E = O(1)+O(4)^2, reproducing the established hyperelliptic value; then h^0(Sym^2E(-6)) = 9 while the target of (1.1) twisted by O(-6) has h^0 = 12-6+1 = 7, so h^0(F(-6)) >= 2 and F is unbalanced. This re-derives ATT-0088/CLM-0088-2 and corroborates FND-0125 inside the present framework.

## 3. The quadric criterion

Keep (H3). Twisting (1.1) by O(-6) and taking sections identifies h^0(F(-6)) with the kernel of

  (3.1)  mu: H^0(P1, Sym^2 E(-6)) -> H^0(C, A_C^2 tensor gamma^*O(-6)) = H^0(C, omega_C^2(-2D)) = H^0(L^2),

since L^2 = omega_C^2(-2D). Fix a splitting of E and compute both sides monomially, using (1.4) to name the restrictions.

*Case E = O(3)^3.* Let y_1,y_2,y_3 be generators of the three summands; they form a basis of M_{-3}, i.e. their restrictions form a basis of H^0(L). Then Sym^2E(-6) = O^6 with basis the monomials y_iy_j, so H^0(Sym^2E(-6)) = Sym^2 M_{-3} and mu is exactly the multiplication map Sym^2 H^0(L) -> H^0(L^2). Hence h^0(F(-6)) = c := dim ker(Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)).

*Case E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4).* Let x,y,z generate the summands, so x in M_{-2}, y in M_{-3}, z in M_{-4}, and let s_0,s_1 be a basis of H^0(O_{P1}(1)). Then Sym^2E(-6) = O(-2)+O(-1)+O(0)^2+O(1)+O(2) with the seven-dimensional space of sections spanned by xz, y^2, s_iyz (two), s_is_jz^2 (three). Write xi, eta, zeta, d_i for the restrictions of x,y,z,s_i; thus zeta spans the one-dimensional H^0(omega_C(-2D)), d_0,d_1 span H^0(O_C(D)), M_{-3} = H^0(L) = <eta> + zeta*H^0(O_C(D)), and M_{-2} = H^0(omega_C) = <xi> + H^0(O_C(D))*H^0(L), the latter subspace being the image of the multiplication H^0(D) tensor H^0(L) -> H^0(omega_C), of dimension 6-1 = 5 by the base-point-free pencil trick (its kernel is H^0(L-D) = H^0(omega_C(-2D)), one-dimensional). Since Sym^2H^0(L) is spanned by eta^2, eta*zeta*d_i, zeta^2 d_id_j, the image of mu is <xi*zeta> + image(Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)) and therefore

  (3.2)  h^0(F(-6)) = 7 - dim image(mu) = c + eps,  eps = 1 if xi*zeta lies in image(Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)), else 0.

The freedom in the splitting replaces x by a unit multiple plus (linear)*y + (quadratic)*z, i.e. replaces xi by a unit multiple modulo H^0(D)*H^0(L); since (H^0(D)*H^0(L))*zeta = (H^0(D)*zeta)*H^0(L) is contained in H^0(L)*H^0(L), the class of xi*zeta modulo the image is well defined, so eps is independent of all choices. With (1.2) this proves (A1):

  (3.3)  b = 5 + c + eps  (eps := 0 when h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = 0),  and (BAL) <=> c = 0 and eps = 0.

Because H^0(L) is three-dimensional, c is the number of independent conics in P2 = P(H^0(L)^vee) whose pullback vanishes on C; when L is base-point-free this is the number of conics containing psi_L(C).

## 4. Three exclusions

**(4a) Trigonal with L = T^2 is unbalanced.** Suppose C carries a g^1_3 T with L = T^2. Then h^0(T) = 2 and pullback along psi_T:C->P1 is injective on sections, so H^0(L) contains psi_T^*H^0(O_{P1}(2)), which is three-dimensional, hence equals it. The Veronese relation is a nonzero element of ker(Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)), so c >= 1 and b >= 6 by (3.3): F is not balanced.

**(4b) (BAL) forces L base-point-free.** Assume (BAL) and (H3) and suppose p is a base point, so h^0(L(-p)) = 3 with deg L(-p) = 5. If L(-p) had a base point q, then L(-p-q) would be a degree-four bundle with three sections, i.e. Clifford equality with degree not in {0,10}, forcing C hyperelliptic, excluded in Section 2. So A := L(-p) is a base-point-free g^2_5; the induced psi_A:C->P2 is nondegenerate (three independent sections), and its degree divides 5, so it is 1 or 5; degree 5 would make the image a line, contradicting nondegeneracy. Hence psi_A is birational onto a plane quintic whose geometric genus is 6, equal to its arithmetic genus, so the quintic is smooth and C is a smooth plane quintic with A = O_C(H), omega_C = O_C(2H), L = O_C(H+p), D = O_C(H-p). Now compute (3.3). First h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = h^0(O_C(2p)) = 1 (non-hyperelliptic), so E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4) and zeta is the section with divisor 2p, i.e. s_p^2 for the canonical section s_p of O_C(p). Second, H^0(L) = s_p H^0(O_C(H)) because h^0(H+p) = h^0(H) = 3, and Sym^2H^0(O_C(H))->H^0(O_C(2H)) is injective (a smooth plane quintic lies on no conic) between spaces of dimension 6, hence bijective; therefore c = 0 and image(Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)) = s_p^2 H^0(O_C(2H)). Third, H^0(D)*H^0(L) is the five-dimensional space of conics through p, so xi may be taken to be a conic Q with Q(p) nonzero, and then xi*zeta = s_p^2 Q lies in s_p^2H^0(O_C(2H)), i.e. eps = 1 and b = 6. So F = O(3)+O(6) is unbalanced, contradicting (BAL). Hence L is base-point-free. (This proves the base-point-freeness that ATT-0088/CLM-0088-4 explicitly did not claim, and it independently corroborates FND-0130 and the base-point-freeness input of FND-0134; note that the argument also shows that the fixed part of |L| is reduced of degree at most one, recovering CLM-0088-4.)

**(4c) Hyperelliptic is unbalanced.** Section 2.

## 5. The dichotomy (A2)

Assume (BAL) and (H3). By (3.3), c = 0 and eps = 0. By (4b), L is base-point-free, so psi_L:C->P2 is a morphism; it is nondegenerate, its image X' is a reduced irreducible curve, and H^0(O_{P2}(1)) -> H^0(L) is an isomorphism, so |L| is precisely the family of pullbacks of lines and |L| is canonically the dual plane. Let m = deg psi_L, so deg X' = 6/m and m divides 6. Since c = 0, no conic contains X', hence deg X' >= 3 and m <= 2.

If m = 1, psi_L is birational onto a plane sextic whose normalization is C: case (a).

If m = 2, then deg X' = 3. Because C is normal and C -> X' is finite dominant, it factors through the normalization X'' of X', and C->X'' has degree two. If X' were singular it would be rational, X'' = P1, and C would be hyperelliptic, contradicting Section 2. So X' is a smooth plane cubic E', C->E' =: phi is a bielliptic structure, and L = phi^*O_{E'}(1) with deg O_{E'}(1) = 3. Then omega_C = phi^*(omega_{E'} tensor delta) = phi^*delta where delta^2 = O_{E'}(B) for the branch divisor B (Riemann-Hurwitz gives deg B = 10 and deg delta = 5), so D = omega_C - L = phi^*(delta - O_{E'}(1)) = phi^*A' with deg A' = 2; since h^0(D) = 2 = h^0(A') and pullbacks of sections of A' are among the sections of D, the pencil |D| is phi^*|A'| and gamma factors as q o phi with q = phi_{|A'|} of degree two: case (b), and gamma is non-primitive through a positive-genus intermediate curve.

Finally, in case (b) h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = h^0(phi^*(delta-2A')) = h^0(delta-2A') + h^0(-2A') = 1 + 0 = 1, because a degree-one line bundle on an elliptic curve has exactly one section; hence h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = 0 forces case (a). The trigonal, plane-quintic and hyperelliptic exclusions are (4a),(4b),(4c). This proves (A2).

## 6. Both cases occur (A3)

**(i) Every bielliptic-composed pencil is balanced.** Let phi:C->E' be a smooth bielliptic genus-six double cover, with branch divisor B of degree 10 on the elliptic curve E' and delta of degree 5 satisfying delta^2 = O(B), so phi_*O_C = O + delta^{-1}, omega_C = phi^*delta, and O_C(R) = phi^*delta for the ramification divisor R. Pick any A' in Pic^2(E'); it is base-point-free (a base point would give a degree-one bundle with two sections), so q := phi_{|A'|}:E'->P1 has degree two and gamma := q o phi has degree four with D = phi^*A'. Set N' := delta tensor A'^{-1} of degree 3. Then:

- h^0(D) = h^0(A') + h^0(A' tensor delta^{-1}) = 2 + 0 = 2 and h^0(L) = h^0(phi^*N') = h^0(N') + h^0(N' tensor delta^{-1}) = 3 + 0 = 3, so (H3) holds and H^0(L) = phi^*H^0(N') consists of invariant sections;
- h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = 1 as in Section 5, with generator zeta = phi^*t invariant, t spanning H^0(T'), T' := delta tensor A'^{-2} of degree one; so E = O(2)+O(3)+O(4) by (2.1);
- c = 0: the multiplication Sym^2H^0(N')->H^0(N'^2) is injective because |N'| embeds E' as a smooth plane cubic, which lies on no conic, and it has bijective source and target of dimension 6; pullback along the surjective phi is injective on sections, so Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2) is injective;
- eps = 0: H^0(D)*H^0(L) = phi^*(H^0(A')*H^0(N')) = phi^*H^0(delta) since A' tensor N' = delta and the base-point-free pencil trick gives image of dimension 2*3-h^0(N'-A') = 6-1 = 5 = h^0(delta); as H^0(omega_C) = H^0(phi^*delta) = phi^*H^0(delta) + (one-dimensional anti-invariant line), xi may be chosen anti-invariant. Then xi*zeta is a nonzero anti-invariant section of L^2, while image(Sym^2H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)) = phi^*H^0(N'^2) consists of invariant sections; in characteristic zero invariant and anti-invariant parts intersect in 0, so xi*zeta is not in the image.

By (3.3), h^0(F(-6)) = 0 and F = O(4)+O(5): the pair is balanced, and it is of type (b). Since bielliptic genus-six curves exist (take B a general reduced member of |delta^2|), case (b) is nonempty. This settles affirmatively the open frontier question, and it does so universally over the whole bielliptic-composed family, not by a finite computation. It is consistent with, and strictly beyond, the recorded constraint that constancy of h^0(omega_C(-D)) excludes only the hyperelliptic-composed case: that constraint says such pencils are not excluded, whereas the computation above shows they are in fact balanced.

**(ii) A type-(a) point.** Let C be a smooth complete intersection of divisors of types (1,2) and (2,2) in P1 x P2 and gamma the first projection. Then [C] = (H_1+2H_2)(2H_1+2H_2) = 6H_1H_2+4H_2^2, so deg gamma = [C].H_1 = 4, omega_C = O_C(1,1) of degree 10 and g = 6; C is canonically embedded by the Segre-very-ample O(1,1), hence non-hyperelliptic, so h^0(D) = 2 by Clifford and h^0(L) = 3 with L = O_C(0,1) of degree 6. Next h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = h^0(O_C(-1,1)) = 0: the Koszul resolution 0->O(-3,-4)->O(-1,-2)+O(-2,-2)->I_C->0 twisted by (-1,1) has H^0 of the middle term zero and H^1(O(-4,-3)) = 0, so H^0(I_C(-1,1)) = 0; and H^1(I_C(-1,1)) = 0 because H^1(O(-2,-1)) = H^1(O(-3,-1)) = 0 and H^2(O(-4,-3)) = 0; since H^0(O_{P1 x P2}(-1,1)) = 0 the restriction sequence gives H^0(O_C(-1,1)) = 0. Hence E = O(3)^3 by (2.1) and eps = 0 by convention, so by (3.3) F is balanced if and only if c = 0. Finally psi_L is the second projection, which is birational: for a general point of P2 the type-(1,2) equation is linear in the P1-coordinate and determines a unique preimage. So X' is a plane sextic, c = 0, F = O(4)+O(5), and the pair is balanced of type (a). (This independently confirms the pinned reusable computation recording F = O(4)+O(5) and E^vee = O(-3)^3 for this curve; the existence statement here rests on the proof above, not on that computation.)

## 7. Fibrewise monodromy in case (a): the full symmetric group

Assume (BAL), (H3) and case (a). By ATT-0088/CLM-0088-5 the non-reduced locus Delta of |L| is a closed curve and U_C = |L| - Delta is a nonempty dense open of the plane |L|; the ordering scheme Z_C->U_C is a finite etale S_6-torsor, and G_C denotes the image of pi_1(U_C) in S_6 acting on the six points of the universal divisor. By the invariance of the geometric fundamental group under extension of algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, we may take k = C. Write J = {(x,l) : x in C, l in |L|, x in psi_L^*l}, a P1-bundle over C, hence irreducible and smooth of dimension two; J -> |L| is the six-sheeted universal divisor, finite etale exactly over U_C.

**Transitivity.** J is irreducible, hence so is the open subset lying over U_C; therefore G_C is transitive.

**2-transitivity.** Let J_2 -> U_C be the cover of ordered pairs of distinct points of the divisor, finite etale of degree 30 over the smooth surface U_C, hence smooth of pure dimension two. Consider the locally closed subset of J_2 where psi_L(x_1) is not equal to psi_L(x_2). On it the projection (x_1,x_2,l) -> (x_1,x_2) is injective, because l is then the unique line through the two distinct image points; so this subset is isomorphic to an open subset of C x C and is irreducible, and it is nonempty (choose a general line). Its complement in J_2 lies over the finitely many pairs of points of C with the same image (psi_L is birational, so those are finitely many), and hence has dimension at most one. A pure two-dimensional scheme with an irreducible dense open subset is irreducible, so J_2 is irreducible and G_C is 2-transitive; in particular G_C is primitive.

**A transposition.** In characteristic zero psi_L is generically immersive, so let q run over the dense open of C where the differential is nonzero and let l_q be the tangent line of the branch at psi_L(q). For general q: the contact order at q is exactly two (flexes are finite because X' is not a line); l_q is tangent at no other point (by reflexivity the conormal map is birational onto the dual curve X'^*, so multiply tangent lines are finite in number); l_q passes through none of the finitely many points where psi_L fails to be immersive or is not injective (for each such point x_0, the tangent lines through x_0 correspond to finitely many q); and l_q is a general, hence smooth, point of the reduced irreducible dual curve X'^*, and lies on no other component of Delta (the remaining components are the finitely many lines dual to the non-immersive points). Thus psi_L^*l_q = 2q + p_1 + ... + p_4 with five distinct points, Delta is smooth at l_q, and near l_q the cover J -> |L| is the disjoint union of four unbranched sheets and a degree-two map of smooth surfaces branched exactly along the smooth Delta, which is locally the standard double cover; the meridian of Delta at l_q therefore acts as a single transposition, which lies in G_C.

By Jordan's theorem a primitive subgroup of S_6 containing a transposition is S_6, so G_C = S_6. (This agrees with, and reproves in the case at hand, the classical uniform position theorem for a nondegenerate irreducible plane curve.) A finite etale S_6-torsor with full monodromy is connected; Z_C is smooth of dimension two over k, hence normal, so Z_C is irreducible of dimension two. This proves the first half of (A4).

## 8. Fibrewise monodromy in case (b): imprimitivity and at least fifteen components

Assume (BAL), (H3) and case (b), with phi:C->E' and L = phi^*N'. Since H^0(L) = phi^*H^0(N') (Section 6(i)), phi^* induces an isomorphism |N'| -> |L| of planes, and every member of |L| is phi^*(a member of |N'|). Consequently the universal divisor of |L| is the fibre product

  J = C x_{E'} J'',  J'' := {(x',l) : x' in l-section of |N'|},

so J -> |L| factors as the degree-two map J -> J'' followed by the degree-three map J'' -> |L|. Restricting to U_C, the six points of each divisor are partitioned canonically into the three fibres of phi (a member of |L| is reduced exactly when the corresponding member of |N'| is reduced and misses the branch divisor, in which case its preimage consists of three free phi-orbits). Monodromy preserves a partition defined by an intermediate covering, so G_C lies in the stabilizer of that partition, a conjugate of S_2 wr S_3, of order 48. For a right S_6-torsor the connected components correspond to the cosets of the monodromy group, so Z_C has [S_6 : G_C] >= 720/48 = 15 connected components; in particular Z_C is disconnected, hence reducible. This proves the second half of (A4). No claim is made here about the exact value of G_C.

The contrast with Section 7 is exactly the failure of 2-transitivity: in case (b) the pair cover J_2 splits according to whether the two points lie in the same phi-fibre.

## 9. Components and dimensions over a base (Part B)

Let S be reduced locally Noetherian over k with a family satisfying (CE),(BAL),(N). By ATT-0088/CLM-0088-8 (dual-confirmed by REV-0139 and REV-0142, and stated there exactly for reduced S), pi_*L is locally free of rank three, AJ = P_S(pi_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P2-bundle, its reduced-support open U is S-smooth of pure relative dimension two and surjective onto S, Z is canonically the S_6-torsor of orderings over U and coincides with the CE evaluation-failure scheme of ATT-0065, and Z->S is smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two. Base change identifies the geometric fibres of Z->U with the fibrewise torsors of Sections 7 and 8.

(B1) Since U->S is smooth surjective with irreducible (hence connected) geometric fibres, U is connected whenever S is: a decomposition of U into two disjoint nonempty opens would push forward to a decomposition of S, because smooth morphisms are open and no fibre can meet both parts. Functoriality of the fibre functor gives, for every geometric point b of S, an inclusion G_b = image(pi_1(U_b)) contained in image(pi_1(U)) = H. If some fibre is of type (a) then G_b = S_6 by Section 7, so H = S_6 and Z is connected. If moreover S is normal and irreducible, then Z is normal (smooth over a normal base) and connected, hence irreducible; the same holds for U; and for S of finite type over k the imported dimension formula gives dim Z = dim S + 2. Note that this route uses normality explicitly, as the recorded constraint on upgrading orbit counts to component counts requires.

(B2) If every geometric fibre is of type (a), then every geometric fibre of Z->S is irreducible by Section 7. In that situation no normality hypothesis is needed. Indeed Z->S is flat of finite presentation, so going-down places the generic point of every irreducible component of Z over a generic point of a component of S. Fix an irreducible component S_alpha with its reduced structure and put Z_alpha = Z x_S S_alpha; the topological space of Z is the union of those of the Z_alpha. For irreducible S_alpha with generic point eta, the fibre Z_eta is irreducible; every component of Z_alpha dominates S_alpha, so its generic point lies in Z_eta; writing Z_eta as the finite union of its intersections with the components shows Z_eta is contained in one component, and then every other component contains its own generic point inside Z_eta, hence is contained in that one; so Z_alpha is irreducible. Distinct components S_alpha give distinct maximal Z_alpha because Z_alpha surjects onto S_alpha. Hence the irreducible components of Z (and likewise of U) correspond bijectively to those of S, with dim = dim S_alpha + 2 for S of finite type over k. Equivalently, in the [S_6 : H] component formula one has H = S_6.

(B3) If some geometric fibre b is of type (b), then Z_b has at least fifteen connected components by Section 8. Hence no statement of the form 'the fibrewise monodromy is full' and no fibrewise component count is available over any base meeting the bielliptic-composed locus, even though (B1) may still give a connected, indeed irreducible, total space. Both existence statements of Section 6 show that the two regimes really occur inside the balanced locus, so this is not a vacuous distinction. For orientation only, a coarse parameter count for the bielliptic-composed pairs is 1 (elliptic curve) + 1 (delta in Pic^5) + 9 (branch divisor in |delta^2|) + 1 (A' in Pic^2) - 1 (translations) = 11, the fibres of this parametrization being finite because a genus-six curve has at most one bielliptic involution: two independent bielliptic maps would give g <= 2*1+2*1+(2-1)(2-1) = 5 by Castelnuovo-Severi, and a common intermediate factor has degree dividing 2 and at least 2, hence equals both maps. No closedness, density, stack-dimension or codimension claim is attached to this count.

## 10. Stabilizers, pencil recovery and faithfulness

**(A5) fibrewise.** Assume (BAL) and (H3), and let Gamma be effective with O_C(Gamma) = L. Then omega_C(-Gamma) = omega_C tensor L^{-1} = O_C(D), whose complete linear system is the base-point-free pencil |D| of degree four defining gamma (h^0(D) = 2 by Section 2, and |D| is base-point-free because it is the pencil of fibres of gamma). Hence gamma is canonically reconstructed from the pair (C,Gamma) as the morphism attached to |omega_C(-Gamma)|, up to a unique automorphism of P1. If sigma in Aut(C) satisfies sigma(Gamma) = Gamma then sigma preserves omega_C(-Gamma), hence permutes |omega_C(-Gamma)| = |D|, hence there is a unique tau in Aut(P1) with gamma o sigma = tau o gamma. Therefore Aut(C,Gamma) = Aut(C,gamma,Gamma). This proves the equality rather than transporting a PGL_2 argument for one group to the other, which is exactly what the recorded stabilizer constraint forbids: the two groups are here shown to coincide, and the identification is what licenses using either.

**Nontrivial inertia does occur.** In case (b), every member of |L| is phi^*(a member of |N'|) and is therefore invariant under the bielliptic involution sigma, so sigma lies in Aut(C,Gamma) for every Gamma in |L|; on a reduced Gamma it acts as a product of three disjoint transpositions (a reduced Gamma misses the ramification divisor), so it does not fix any ordered point. For ordered points the situation is different, and nontrivial stabilizers exist inside the balanced locus. Let C'' be a general genus-two curve with hyperelliptic class A' = omega_{C''}, let delta in Pic^3(C'') be general (so delta - A' is not effective, hence |delta| is base-point-free of degree three), let B be a general reduced member of |delta^2| (degree six), let phi:C->C'' be the double cover branched along B, and let gamma = phi_{|A'|} o phi have degree four. Then: g(C) = 6 by Riemann-Hurwitz; O_C(R) = phi^*delta for the ramification divisor R (six distinct points, each fixed by the covering involution sigma) and omega_C = phi^*(A' tensor delta); D = phi^*A' with h^0(D) = h^0(A') + h^0(A' tensor delta^{-1}) = 2+0 = 2; L = omega_C(-D) = phi^*delta = O_C(R), so h^0(L) = h^0(delta) + h^0(O_{C''}) = 2+1 = 3 and (H3) holds; h^0(omega_C(-2D)) = h^0(phi^*(delta - A')) = h^0(delta-A') + h^0(-A') = 0, so E = O(3)^3 and by (3.3) the pair is balanced if and only if no conic contains psi_L(C), i.e. (Section 5) if and only if C is not trigonal with L = T^2. If it were, then R, being a member of |L| = |2T|, would be a sum of two fibres of the trigonal pencil; the trigonal pencil is unique (two g^1_3's are non-independent by Castelnuovo-Severi and then equal by the divisibility step), so sigma preserves it and it descends to a degree-three pencil on C'' whose two corresponding fibres sum to B, with twice its class linearly equivalent to delta^2. For fixed C'' and delta these constraints confine B to a two-dimensional subset of the four-dimensional |delta^2|, so a general B avoids them. Hence for general B the pair is balanced, Gamma := R is a reduced member of |L|, and sigma is a nontrivial element of Aut(C,Gamma) = Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) fixing each of the six points of Gamma. Therefore the stabilizer of an ordered point of the failure locus is not always trivial, and no clause asserting generically or universally trivial inertia is available; this realizes inside the balanced locus the possibility flagged by the recorded constraint that an automorphism of a genus-six curve can fix six marked points. (Incidentally this is a second family of balanced non-primitive pencils, with intermediate genus two; the intermediate-genus-three case is not decided here.)

**(B4) families.** Let T be a reduced S-scheme and Gamma a relative effective divisor in C_T with O(Gamma) = L_T tensor pi^*M. Fibrewise omega_{C/T}(-Gamma) = O(D) tensor (a line from the base), so h^0 is constantly two; Grauert over the reduced T makes V := p_{T*}(omega_{C_T/T}(-Gamma)) locally free of rank two and compatible with base change, and the evaluation p_T^*V -> omega_{C_T/T}(-Gamma) is surjective because it is fibrewise surjective (base-point-freeness of |D|) and Nakayama applies. The resulting T-morphism C_T -> P_T(V^vee) is finite of fibre degree four, and the natural map s_*O_P(1) -> V is an isomorphism (both are rank two, compatible with base change, and the map is a fibrewise isomorphism since H^0(C,gamma^*O(1)) = H^0(O_{P1}(1)) by h^0(E^vee(1)) = 0), so there is an isomorphism of P1-bundles P = P_T(V^vee) over T carrying gamma_T to the constructed morphism; it is unique because gamma_T is surjective. Hence the assignment (C,gamma,Gamma) -> (C,Gamma) is injective up to isomorphism on reduced T-points and induces isomorphisms on automorphism groups (an automorphism of (C_T,Gamma) preserves omega(-Gamma), hence lifts uniquely to the P1-bundle), i.e. it is fully faithful on reduced T-points. This is deliberately not upgraded to a monomorphism of stacks: the recorded constraint requires full faithfulness over every base scheme, including nonreduced ones, where Grauert is unavailable; that extension, and with it closedness, quasi-finiteness, image and codimension in M_{6,6}, is left open.

## 11. Scope: what is proved, what is imported, what remains

Proved here from standard theorems: the exact sequences (1.1) and (1.3) and the graded identification (1.4); the splitting-type dichotomy (2.1); the quadric criterion (3.3) with its well-definedness; the exclusions of the hyperelliptic-composed, trigonal-with-L=2T and base-point (smooth plane quintic) cases, hence base-point-freeness of L on the balanced locus; the dichotomy (A2) and the implication that E = O(3)^3 forces type (a); balancedness of every bielliptic-composed pencil and of the (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection, so both types occur; the fibrewise monodromy computations G_C = S_6 in type (a) and imprimitivity with at least fifteen components in type (b); the family-level statements (B1)-(B3) about connectedness, irreducibility, component correspondence and dimension; and the stabilizer equality with its family-level full faithfulness on reduced bases plus an explicit nontrivial ordered stabilizer.

Imported inside their verified scope: the identification of the CE evaluation-failure scheme with the Abel-Jacobi incidence and its Fitting scheme structure (ATT-0065, REV-0108, REV-0109); the h^0-stratification and torsor formalism (ATT-0066, REV-0110, REV-0116); emptiness of the jump stratum (ATT-0086, REV-0135, REV-0138); h^0(L) = 3, density of the reduced-support open, and the reduced-base projective-bundle/torsor/smoothness model with its dimension formula (ATT-0088, REV-0139, REV-0142). SRC-0004 supplies only the CE convention and the two degree formulas.

Computational hypotheses: none. No point count, database, or finite experiment is used to establish a universal statement; the two families in Section 6 and the family in Section 10 support existence statements only, and each is verified by a proof valid for the whole family rather than for one member.

Gaps, stated as such: irreducibility (and normality) of the balanced tetragonal base is an unproved hypothesis of (B1) and (B2), and is not inferred from irreducibility of the classical Hurwitz space; (N) remains an explicit hypothesis; the exact monodromy group in type (b) is not determined; the intermediate-genus-three non-primitive case is not decided; nonreduced and stack bases are untreated, so the passage from full faithfulness on reduced T-points to a stack monomorphism, and all statements about closedness, quasi-finiteness, image, image dimension and codimension in M_{6,6}, remain open; unbalanced CE strata are unconstructed; and nothing here bears directly on weights, purity or Tate type, so RED-0001 is untouched. The bielliptic sublocus identified in Section 6(i) is, however, the precise place where a downstream Tate-type argument must work: over it the ordered failure locus is disconnected and its geometry is governed by a varying elliptic curve, whose weight-one cohomology is not Tate. That is recorded as a located risk for C66-TATE-SUPPORT and C66-CEX-LOCAL, not as a claim about the exact target.

Affirmative resolution of the open frontier question whether a non-primitive degree-four pencil through a positive-genus intermediate curve can have balanced CE splitting: every bielliptic genus-six curve with gamma factoring through its elliptic quotient is balanced, universally over that family and not by a finite computation. A second balanced non-primitive family (intermediate genus two) is also exhibited.

Base-point-freeness of L on the whole balanced locus, proved by the same criterion (the plane-quintic case is excluded through the eps term), closing the point that ATT-0088 explicitly left neither asserted nor denied, and exclusion of the trigonal locus with L = 2T.

Determination of the fibrewise finite-cover behaviour: full S_6 geometric monodromy on the birational (type a) locus, by an elementary proof (2-transitivity from the pair incidence, one transposition from a simple tangency, Jordan) rather than by quoting uniform position; and imprimitive monodromy of order at most 48 with at least fifteen components on the bielliptic locus, which shows that fibrewise full monodromy is false on the balanced locus while total-space irreducibility can still be obtained.

A normality-free component correspondence for the ordered failure locus when all fibres are of type (a), obtained from smoothness with geometrically irreducible fibres rather than from an orbit count, plus the normal-base variant needing only one good fibre.

Determination of the stabilizer question: Aut(C,Gamma) = Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) by functorial recovery of the pencil as |omega_C(-Gamma)|, with full faithfulness on reduced T-points, together with an explicit balanced ordered point whose stabilizer is a nontrivial involution fixing all six marked points, so that no trivial-inertia clause is available.

summary: Fibrewise criterion: under (CE)+(N)+(h^0(L)=3), the maximal splitting degree of the CE relations bundle is b = 5 + h^0(F(-6)) and h^0(F(-6)) equals the number of conics through the residual g^2_6 model psi_L(C) plus an explicit 0/1 correction present only when h^0(omega_C(-2D))=1. Hence (BAL) is equivalent to a conic-containment statement, which (i) excludes the trigonal locus with L = 2T, (ii) proves that L is base-point-free on the whole balanced locus (the plane-quintic case is excluded by the correction term), and (iii) reduces the balanced geometry to a sharp dichotomy: either psi_L is birational onto a plane sextic (type a), or C is bielliptic and gamma factors through the elliptic quotient (type b). Both types are nonempty: every bielliptic-composed degree-four pencil is balanced, which answers affirmatively the open frontier question whether a non-primitive pencil through a positive-genus intermediate curve can be balanced, and a (1,2)-(2,2) complete intersection in P1 x P2 gives a type-(a) point. Consequences for C66-GEO-COMP: in type (a) the fibrewise geometric monodromy of the ordered S_6-cover is the full S_6 (2-transitivity from the pair incidence, a transposition from a simple tangency, Jordan), so the fibre of the ordered failure locus is irreducible; in type (b) the monodromy is imprimitive of order at most 48 and the fibre has at least 15 components, so fibrewise full monodromy is false on the balanced locus. Over a base, this gives a normality-free component correspondence when all fibres are of type (a), and irreducibility of Z whenever the base is normal irreducible and contains one type-(a) fibre. Finally Aut(C,Gamma) = Aut(C,gamma,Gamma) by functorial recovery of the pencil as |omega_C(-Gamma)|, with full faithfulness on reduced T-points, and there is an explicit balanced ordered point with nontrivial Z/2 inertia fixing all six marked points, so no trivial-stabilizer clause holds.

theorem_scope.base: algebraically closed field of characteristic zero; Part A is absolute (single geometric fibre); Part B assumes S reduced locally Noetherian, and finite type over k where dimensions are asserted

theorem_statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. PART A (fibrewise). Let C be a smooth projective connected genus-6 curve over k, gamma:C->P1 finite flat of degree four, E the Tschirnhausen bundle (gamma_*O_C = O + E^vee), p:X=P(E^vee)->P1 with p_*O_X(1)=E, i:C->X the Casnati-Ekedahl embedding and F the rank-two relations bundle. Assume (CE) the standard degree-four CE resolution 0->O_X(-4) tensor p^*det F->O_X(-2) tensor p^*F->I_C->0, and (N) O_X(1)|_C = omega_{C/P1} tensor gamma^*A for some A in Pic(P1). Put D=gamma^*(pt), L=omega_C(-D), and assume (H3) h^0(L)=3. Then: (A0) A=O, so O_X(1)|_C=omega_{C/P1}=:A_C; deg E=deg F=9; F=p_*(I_C tensor O_X(2))=ker(Sym^2 E->gamma_*(A_C^2)); F=O(a)+O(b) with a+b=9, a<=b, and b=5+h^0(F(-6)), so F is balanced if and only if h^0(F(-6))=0. (A1) C is not hyperelliptic, h^0(omega_C(-2D)) is 0 or 1, and E=O(3)^3 in the first case, E=O(2)+O(3)+O(4) in the second. Writing c:=dim ker(Sym^2 H^0(L)->H^0(L^2)), one has h^0(F(-6))=c when h^0(omega_C(-2D))=0, and h^0(F(-6))=c+eps when h^0(omega_C(-2D))=1, where eps in {0,1} is 1 exactly when xi*zeta lies in the image of Sym^2 H^0(L)->H^0(L^2), zeta spanning H^0(omega_C(-2D)) and xi being any element of H^0(omega_C) outside the five-dimensional subspace H^0(O_C(D))*H^0(L); eps does not depend on the choice of xi. (A2) If in addition (BAL) F=O(4)+O(5), then Sym^2 H^0(L)->H^0(L^2) is injective, L is base-point-free, |L| is the pullback of the system of lines under psi_L:C->P2=P(H^0(L)^vee), and exactly one of: (a) deg psi_L=1 and psi_L is birational onto a plane sextic of geometric genus six; (b) deg psi_L=2, the image is a smooth plane cubic E', C is bielliptic by phi:C->E' with L=phi^*O_{E'}(1), and gamma=q o phi with q:E'->P1 of degree two. In particular C is not hyperelliptic, C is not trigonal with L=T^2 for a g^1_3 T, and C is not a smooth plane quintic with gamma the projection from a point of C; moreover h^0(omega_C(-2D))=0 forces case (a). (A3) Both cases occur: (i) for every smooth bielliptic genus-six phi:C->E' and every degree-two A' in Pic(E'), the pair (C, gamma=q o phi) with q=phi_{|A'|} satisfies h^0(L)=3, h^0(omega_C(-2D))=1 and, under (CE)+(N), F=O(4)+O(5); (ii) for C a smooth complete intersection of divisors of types (1,2) and (2,2) in P1 x P2 with gamma the first projection, h^0(L)=3, h^0(omega_C(-2D))=0, psi_L is birational and, under (CE)+(N), F=O(4)+O(5). (A4) Assume (BAL) and let Delta be the non-reduced locus of |L|, U_C=|L|-Delta (nonempty, dense, open), and Z_C->U_C the finite etale S_6-torsor of orderings of the universal divisor. In case (a) the geometric monodromy group G_C = image(pi_1(U_C)->S_6) equals S_6 and Z_C is irreducible, smooth of dimension two; in case (b) G_C preserves the partition of each fibre into the three fibres of phi, hence lies in a conjugate of S_2 wr S_3 of order 48, and Z_C has at least 15 connected components, so Z_C is reducible. (A5) Assume (BAL). For every effective Gamma with O_C(Gamma)=L one has omega_C(-Gamma)=O_C(D), |omega_C(-Gamma)| is the complete base-point-free pencil defining gamma, and Aut(C,Gamma)=Aut(C,gamma,Gamma):={sigma in Aut(C): sigma(Gamma)=Gamma and gamma o sigma = tau o gamma for some tau in Aut(P1)}. In case (b) the bielliptic involution lies in Aut(C,Gamma) for every Gamma in |L| and acts on a reduced Gamma as a product of three disjoint transpositions. Furthermore there exist balanced pairs satisfying (CE),(N),(H3) - namely C->C'' a double cover of a general genus-two curve with general branch divisor, gamma the composite with the hyperelliptic map of C'' - and a reduced Gamma in |L| (the ramification divisor) admitting a nontrivial involution in Aut(C,Gamma) fixing all six points of Gamma; hence stabilizers of ordered points of the failure locus are not always trivial. PART B (families; S reduced). Let S be a reduced locally Noetherian k-scheme carrying a family satisfying (CE),(BAL),(N) as in ATT-0088, AJ=P_S(pi_*L), U the reduced-support open of AJ, and Z the CE evaluation-failure scheme, so that (ATT-0088, CLM-0088-8) U->S and Z->S are smooth surjective of pure relative dimension two and Z->U is a finite etale S_6-torsor. Then: (B1) if S is connected and at least one geometric fibre is of type (a), then pi_1(U)->S_6 is surjective and Z is connected; if moreover S is normal and irreducible then U and Z are irreducible, and if S is of finite type over k then dim Z = dim S + 2. (B2) if every geometric fibre is of type (a), then Z->S has geometrically irreducible fibres and, with no normality hypothesis, the irreducible components of Z and of U are in bijection with those of S, each of dimension dim S_alpha + 2 for S of finite type over k. (B3) if some geometric fibre is of type (b), the corresponding fibre of Z->S has at least 15 connected components; so no fibrewise full-S_6 statement and no fibrewise component count is available over a base meeting the bielliptic-composed locus. (B4) for every reduced S-scheme T and every relative effective divisor Gamma in C_T with O(Gamma)=L_T tensor pi^*M, the sheaf V:=p_{T*}(omega_{C_T/T}(-Gamma)) is locally free of rank two and compatible with base change, its evaluation p_T^*V->omega_{C_T/T}(-Gamma) is surjective, and the induced T-morphism C_T->P_T(V^vee) recovers gamma_T up to a unique isomorphism of P1-bundles over T; consequently the forgetful assignment (C,gamma,Gamma) -> (C,Gamma) is fully faithful on reduced T-points. No assertion is made for nonreduced T, for stack bases, for unbalanced CE strata, for closedness, image, or codimension in M_{6,6}, or about any Hodge, weight, purity or Tate property.
